Concise Clinical Note

Consult Summary:
54-yo male developed acute shortness of breath, chest tightness, lip tingling, and blotchy rash within 15 min of a wasp sting—high concern for early anaphylaxis; advised immediate ambulance transfer and antihistamine.

History:
• Presenting complaint: Breathing difficulty beginning ~15 min after wasp sting while gardening.  
• Symptoms: shallow breaths, chest tightness, tingling sensation in lips, blotchy skin rash. Denies throat closing; no prior similar reaction.  
• Pertinent negatives: No known throat swelling, no wheeze mentioned, no prior asthma.  
• PMH: Eczema; history of aerosinusitis when flying.  
• Allergies: Penicillin.  
• Medications: OTC/PRN antihistamines for flying; no regular daily meds.  
• Social/Preventive: Lives with wife (present); nonspecified smoking/alcohol history; gardening outdoors at time of sting.

Examination:
(Remote video; no vitals obtained)  
• General: Alert, speaking in full sentences but reports shallow breathing.  
• Skin: Patient reports blotchy rash.  
• HEENT: Tingling of lips; no reported throat swelling.  
• Chest: Subjective tightness; no auscultation possible.

Impression:
Most likely diagnosis: Early anaphylaxis secondary to wasp sting.  
Supporting: immediate onset after sting, respiratory symptoms, cutaneous reaction, clinician judgment requiring emergency care.  
Alternate considerations:  
1. Systemic allergic urticaria without full anaphylaxis – less likely given respiratory involvement.  
2. Anxiety-related hyperventilation – rash and allergen exposure favor allergic etiology.

Plan:
• Immediate action: Wife to call emergency ambulance (999) rather than private transport.  
• Medications now: Take available oral antihistamine while awaiting EMS.  
• Transport: Leave by ambulance to nearest ED for observation, possible epinephrine, airway support, and monitoring.  
• Education: Warned about potential rapid deterioration and need for prompt treatment.  
• Documentation: Advised to inform ED of penicillin allergy.

Quality checks:

● Missing/expected elements: vital signs, exact site and number of stings, use/availability of epinephrine auto-injector, full medication list, smoking/alcohol history, follow-up once discharged.  
● Conflicts between transcript and DDx: none noted.  
● Transcript quality: Clear but lacks objective vitals/exam; brief history; minor pauses.
